data.description:
Round 4 of the sbek eval left three MAJOR defects unticketed. They sit in three
different surfaces but they are one failure: **the system already holds the
information, and the organizer's surface drops it.** Fixing them together is
cheaper than three separate passes, because the second and third are each one
query and one projection away from the first.

Round-4 evidence lives in `.eval-kit-agent/ROUND4-DIGEST.md` and the judgements
under `.eval-kit-agent/runs/atlas-2026-08-12T23-50-16/judgements/`.

---

## Part 1 — Co-speaker double-booking is never detected (ai-agenda, the worst of the three)

**Symptom, from the judge:** two time-overlapping sessions in different rooms
that share a person are NOT flagged by the conflicts panel when that person is
attached as a `co_speaker` rather than the primary speaker. The panel is
otherwise real and typed; it simply misses this case.

**Why it matters more than its severity line:** the conflicts panel's entire job
is catching what a human scanning a grid would miss. A detector with a silent
blind spot is worse than no detector, because the organizer now trusts it.

**Read this before you start — the obvious fix is already in place.** I traced
the whole path statically and every layer looks correct:

| layer | file | what I found |
|---|---|---|
| role set | `src/lib/conflicts.ts:4-9` | `AGENDA_PARTICIPATION_ROLES` already contains `co_speaker` |
| filter | `src/lib/conflicts.ts:43-56` | `conflictParticipants` / `sharedConflictParticipants` admit every agenda role |
| projection | `src/routes/agenda.queries.ts:371-381` | `SPEAKERS_JSON` uses `audience: "program"` |
| SQL role filter | `src/lib/participants.ts:40-44` | `"program"` applies **no** role filter — all participations pass |
| per-person dedupe | `src/lib/participants.ts:88-96` | dedupes one row *per person*, does not truncate to one speaker |

So do **not** "fix" the role list — it is already right, and a change there will
look like progress while changing nothing.

**Start by writing the failing test**, driving the judge's exact scenario: two
sessions, overlapping times, different rooms, one person primary on the first
and `co_speaker` on the second. Then find where reality diverges. The remaining
candidates, in the order I would check them:

1. The conflict detection that actually renders the panel may not be the
   `agenda.queries.ts` path at all — check what `/agenda-builder`'s
   `LIVE DETECTION — Agenda conflicts` panel calls.
2. `src/lib/auto-place.ts:103,116` uses the same helpers; compare its behaviour
   with the panel's, since one of them may be right.
3. The fixture may not have attached the co-speaker as a `participations` row on
   the second submission — in which case the product is fine and the defect is
   in the evidence. **If that turns out to be the case, say so and close this
   part; do not invent a fix.**

**Acceptance:** a failing-then-passing test reproducing the scenario above, plus
the panel flagging it in a running system (see validation below).

---

## Part 2 — `/onboarding` renders only the conference's original task templates

**Symptom:** the onboarding progress matrix hard-wires its columns to the six
task types the conference started with. A task authored later at
`/settings/tasks` gets **no column**, so it is untrackable at list level even
when it is assigned and completed. In the round-4 evidence a speaker had
completed the new "Confirm participation" task in her portal, and the matrix
showed her collaborator's whole row as em dashes and her new-task state not at
all.

**Filed independently by two areas** — `speaker-management` (major) and
`content-management` (major) — and it is what pushed **CNT-07 from pass to
partial**, so this one is worth a rubric point as well as the fix.

**Where to look:** `src/routes/onboarding.queries.ts:393` reads
`FROM task_templates WHERE event_id = ?`, and `cellFromTask` (~line 209) builds
each cell against a template. The question is whether the column set is derived
from templates only, or from templates ∪ tasks-that-exist. Note that `/files`
gets this right — it is a true speaker × file-task register — and `/onboarding`'s
own `TASK TYPE` filter also finds the new tasks correctly. **Only the matrix
columns are wrong**, which suggests the data is already available to the page.

**Acceptance:** a task authored after conference setup gets a column in the
matrix, its per-speaker cells show real state, and a row with no applicable
tasks is distinguishable from a row whose tasks are merely unstarted.

---

## Part 3 — CSV import destructively overwrites existing speaker profile data

**Symptom:** the Sessionize import overwrites an existing speaker's profile with
the CSV's values, with no field-level merge and no choice offered. In the
evidence, a pre-existing speaker's carefully-written bio was replaced by the
CSV's one-liner. Present in **round 3 as well as round 4**, so this is standing
behaviour, not a recent break.

**Where to look:** `src/lib/sessionize-import.ts:488-497`. `changed` is computed
by comparing every field, then the UPDATE writes `next.*` wholesale. Compare
with the add-speaker path in `src/routes/speakers.routes.ts:~264`, which already
implements the right rule and states it in a comment: *"Add-speaker is an add,
never an erase. When the email resolves to someone the organization already
knows, a field left blank on the form means 'I did not retype this', not 'delete
what the speaker wrote in their portal'."*

**That rule is the product's existing position — the import simply does not
follow it.** The cheapest correct fix is to make the import obey the same rule:
a blank CSV cell never erases a stored value.

**Decide and record:** a *non-blank* CSV cell that disagrees with a stored value
is a genuine product question — last-write-wins, or surface a conflict? The
import already has a per-row outcome table and a Batch undo, so last-write-wins
with an honest row reason is defensible. **State the choice in the PR; do not
leave it implicit.**

**Also here, cheap while you are in the file:** the ROW DETAIL table reports
outcome `created` with reason `matched by normalized email` — the identical
string it shows on `updated` rows. An organizer auditing an import cannot tell
why a row was created. (Filed separately as a minor in round 4.)

---

## Architectural context

- Speaker records are `people` rows (org-scoped). Human properties — bio,
  headshot, title, company, socials — live on `people`; this event's
  participation lives on `participations`. Part 3 is writing to `people`, which
  is why it is destructive across every conference that person speaks at.
- "Who speaks at this conference" is defined once in `src/lib/roster-source.ts`
  (membership ∪ participation-on-a-rostered-submission). Part 1 and Part 2 both
  read populations that derive from it; do not introduce a second definition.
- The suite budget is 45s and the gate 120s. Several agents build here at once,
  so a time-only failure is contention — check load before believing it.

## Validation — required before `pr_open`

Local review is not enough for any of these three; each is a surface the
organizer looks at. Drive the running system:

- **Part 1:** place two overlapping sessions sharing a co-speaker and screenshot
  the conflicts panel flagging it.
- **Part 2:** author a task at `/settings/tasks`, assign it, complete it as the
  speaker, and screenshot the matrix column showing that state.
- **Part 3:** import a CSV with a blank bio cell for an existing speaker and show
  the stored bio survives.

Record evidence with `lattice attach <task> --role validation`. The bar is
"I saw it work," not "I think it should work."

## Scope — what this ticket is NOT

- **Not** the bare-`/portal` conference resolution defect. That is already
  `in_progress` under the two "submitter seat" tickets — leave it alone.
- **Not** the public-surface headshots. Round 4 filed a minor for every avatar
  being an initials monogram; on inspection that is deliberate
  (`src/lib/public-headshots.ts`: *"Deliberately synthetic avatars for the
  published demo roster"*). **No defect. Do not "fix" it.**
- **Not** ABS-09 (reviewer Remind) or ABS-13 (export confirmation) — both were
  root-caused and shipped by the Demo UX agent in PR #165.
data.title: Three round-4 majors: the system holds the information and the organizer's surface drops it

data.body:
Validated in a running local Worker (build 1dc256e7, wrangler dev + c11 embedded browser, seeded AIE NYC demo).

**Part 1 — the co-speaker role was never the bug.** The repro driving the judge's exact co-speaker scenario passes on unfixed `main`. The hole is the other side of the pair: the organizer's **+ Add session** (`/submissions/new`) records one participation, of role `submitter`. Every organizer surface prints that person (the program audience keeps submitters — which is why the judge's publish panel row read `· Marcus Okafor`), while `conflictParticipants` excluded the role, so the detector believed nobody was on that stage. Live proof: created a session owned by Colin Flaherty through + Add session — the record card reads 'Colin Flaherty · Submitter', sole participant — placed it overlapping 'Building Self-Coding Agents', and the panel went 7 → 8 conflicts with 'Colin Flaherty is double-booked across two sessions.'

**Part 2 — the columns were never hard-wired either.** They are derived from `task_templates`, and `speaker_tasks.template_id` is NOT NULL against that table, so every authored task already had a column. It lands at the far right of a grid that scrolls horizontally with no affordance. Authored 'Confirm participation' and 'Speaker agreement' at /settings/tasks: the strip now reads '8 task columns · scroll the grid sideways to reach "Speaker agreement"', both columns render with real per-speaker state (Apr 1, 2027), the speaker column is pinned at left, and a speaker with nothing assigned reads 'No tasks assigned' rather than a row of em dashes.

**Part 3 — decided and stated.** A blank CSV cell keeps the stored value; a filled cell that disagrees is **last-write-wins**, because the import already ships a per-row outcome table and a Batch undo. Imported a CSV for Grace Isford with a blank Bio and Company and a changed Job Title: her 1,244-character portal bio and 'Lux Capital' survived, the title moved to 'General Partner', and ROW DETAIL reads 'matched by normalized email; overwrote title; kept company, bio (blank in CSV)'.

Worth its own ticket, not widened into here: **/submissions/new collects only a submitter** while its own copy says 'This person is recorded as the submitter and speaker-of-record context'. The conflict fix makes the detector agree with what the tile prints, but the record still has no speaking participant until someone adds one.

Code review returned **PASS**, no blocking issues (art_01KZYEXX0EN14RPNMNY5V7DRJF).

**#182 was merged by Atin at 21:03:34Z**, while I was applying the review's first minor. That fix therefore did not land with it and is now open as **#184** (gated green, 63.4s/120s): the speaker column's sticky `left` was a hand-copied duplicate of the select column's width, so a later width change would silently misalign the pinned pair. Both now read one `--select-column-width` token and the contract test asserts the coupling.

**Deserves its own ticket** (second review minor, pre-existing, out of MRQ-164's scope): `sessionize-import.ts` writes `people.email` unconditionally with no blank-preserves-stored guard. An existing person matched **by name** with a blank CSV email column has their real address replaced by a synthetic `speaker+<hash>@example.invalid` placeholder — the same failure class this ticket fixed for title/company/bio, three lines above code it touched. It needs a decision rather than a reflex extension of `merge()`: email is the key the next import matches on, so guarding it changes matching behaviour, not just stored data.

Also still open from earlier: **/submissions/new collects only a submitter** while its copy promises 'submitter and speaker-of-record context'.
